title: Text tools
description: Count, sort and search lines, remove repeats, and pull a column from a file.

exercises.task: Make fruits.txt. Put apple, banana, apple and cherry on four lines in that order.
exercises.hint: In printf, put \n after each fruit, including the last, to start a new line. Use > fruits.txt to save what printf prints.
wc counts things in a file. Use -l (lowercase L) to count lines.

exercises.task: Show the lines of fruits.txt in alphabetical order, keeping repeats.
exercises.hint: Use sort with the file name. It prints the sorted lines on your screen.

exercises.task: Show the sorted fruits again, with each fruit appearing just once. Use sort and uniq together.
exercises.hint: uniq removes repeated lines that are next to each other. Use | to pass the sorted lines from sort to uniq.

exercises.task: Use sort and uniq again to show how many times each fruit appears in fruits.txt.
exercises.hint: Keep the same pipe, and add -c to uniq to show a count next to each fruit.

exercises.task: Show only the lines in fruits.txt that contain the letters 'an' together.
exercises.hint: Give grep the text to look for, then the file to search.

exercises.task: Save the sorted fruit names to unique.txt, with one line for each fruit.
exercises.hint: sort -u sorts and removes repeats in one command. Use > unique.txt to save the result.

exercises.task: Make a comma-separated file called people.csv. Put name,city on the first line, Maya,Halifax on the second, and Leo,Ottawa on the third.
exercises.hint: Use printf with \n after each row, including the last one. Save it with > people.csv.

exercises.task: Show just the first column of people.csv, including the heading 'name'.
exercises.hint: With cut, -d, says the comma separates the columns, and -f1 picks the first column.

done: You just counted lines, sorted and removed repeats, searched for text, and picked a column from a file.
